sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract — Japanese (English Wiktionary edition)
sources.citation: Ylonen, T. (2022). Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data. Proceedings of the 13th Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC), pp. 1395–1403. Data: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/ (Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL).
sources.notes: Wiktionary content under CC BY-SA 4.0 (and GFDL); used under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution to Wiktionary contributors and kaikki.org. Per-entry provenance is the word|pos key in sourceRefs.

sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract — Tiếng Nhật (Vietnamese Wiktionary edition)
sources.citation: Ylonen, T. (2022). Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data. Proceedings of the 13th Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC), pp. 1395–1403. Data: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/ (Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL).
sources.notes: Vietnamese Wiktionary content under CC BY-SA 4.0; the Vietnamese senses are the primary native glosses. Entries whose sense text only redirects ("Xem …") are skipped.

sources.name: FrequencyWords (OpenSubtitles 2018 word frequencies)
sources.citation: hermitdave/FrequencyWords — word frequency lists derived from OpenSubtitles2018 (content CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT). https://github.com/hermitdave/FrequencyWords
sources.notes: README: "MIT License for code, CC-by-sa-4.0 for content". Only the derived counts are used; per-million values are relative to the list total (documented in frequency-stats.json).

sources.name: wordfreq 3.1.1 (Zipf frequencies)
sources.citation: Speer, R. (2022). rspeer/wordfreq: v3.0 (v3.0.2). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7199437 — data CC BY-SA 4.0 (includes Google Books Ngram and SUBTLEX components; see the package README for their acknowledgements).
sources.notes: Exported at acquisition time by scripts/lexicon-etl/export-wordfreq.py from the pinned PyPI package (data CC BY-SA 4.0, code Apache-2.0); the export is `word,zipf` for the top 50,000 words of the `large` list when available. The author discourages dumps that strip attribution — the citation ships in ATTRIBUTIONS.md.

sources.name: OpenJLPT 0.1.0 (JLPT N5–N1 vocabulary, level labels from Jonathan Waller's lists)
sources.citation: OpenJLPT 0.1.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0), https://github.com/evanclan/OpenJLPT — levels from Jonathan Waller's JLPT resources (CC BY), readings/glosses via JMdict (EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0), examples from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
sources.notes: The JLPT publishes no official lists; OpenJLPT's N5–N1 groupings are the community-standard Waller lists (NOTICE.md). Used for the N5/N4 anchor levels only.

sources.name: JMdict (EDRDG) — Japanese–English dictionary (JMdict_e)
sources.citation: JMdict — Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG), CC BY-SA 4.0, https://www.edrdg.org/jmdict/j_jmdict.html; licence statement https://www.edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html
sources.notes: EDRDG licence: attribution on a separate About/Sources screen of the app (not only a launch screen) and the licence files included or linked — the Licences screen lists this entry. Readings (r_ele) and English senses used.

notes: Lexicon ETL v2 (P3a) source manifest for ja: every artifact is downloaded from its official location by the dispatch-only workflow .github/workflows/lexicon-source.yml (or a developer run of scripts/lexicon-etl.ts fetch), hashed, and pinned here; raw dumps are never committed. A retrieval that does not hash to the pin is source-version drift and extract refuses to run (re-pin deliberately with recon). Declared sources whose download could not be completed stay "not-retrieved" with the blocker recorded and can never be cited by a lexeme.
